text.autoconfig.spatialhud.title: Spatial HUD
text.autoconfig.spatialhud.option.guideO: Imagine the selected lower HUD as a flat Minecraft map resting at waist height in front of you. Its default near-horizontal surface is readable from above. It is not controlled by a look-down-angle switch: it stays active whenever any part of the real panel is in the screen and is culled only once the complete surface leaves the field of view or passes behind the camera. Every method now captures and warps the complete selected lower HUD—there is no flat non-warp option. Press F6, F7, or F8 to select Method 1, 2, or 3 instantly; rebind them in Minecraft Controls if they conflict. The full-width green, blue, or red band and a brief action-bar message confirm the active choice. Every method includes the enabled health, armor, hunger, air, experience, held-item, mount, and hotbar roots.
text.autoconfig.spatialhud.option.guideC: Green is a required captured-texture mesh, not the old unwarped root-by-root path. It applies a balanced forced perspective warp to every selected pixel, including health and status bars, while retaining a map-like readable shape. Use it when you want real distortion without the stronger blue exaggeration. The wide green band is a live confirmation that this method is selected.
Method 2 — Blue — Strong Captured Projective Warp

Blue is the default and deliberately forces the strongest on-screen distortion. Spatial HUD makes a private picture of only the selected lower HUD, then maps it across a dense 32 by 24 mesh. The blue band, backing, hotbar slots, health and status bars, icons, and text all share one flat surface, so their farther edge visibly changes size and shape together. It does not capture your inventory, chat, menus, minimap, debug text, or unrelated mod screens.
text.autoconfig.spatialhud.option.guideW: Method 3 — Red — World-Space Texture: a real in-world map

Choose this when you want the panel to exist as a real flat textured surface in the Minecraft world. It uses the same selected lower-HUD source rectangle as blue Method 2, but places it on a physical world quad instead of a GUI-space mesh. Normal game perspective and optional terrain occlusion therefore apply directly. You can decide whether it follows Camera Yaw or Player Body direction. It intentionally shows the last completed HUD picture, so a one-frame delay is normal; persistent flicker or missing texture is not.
text.autoconfig.spatialhud.option.enable: Master switch for Spatial HUD. When disabled, every wrapped vanilla HUD root is immediately delegated back to Minecraft without a pose transform, private capture, or world-space draw. The separate Toggle Spatial HUD keybinding changes this same switch for quick comparison.
text.autoconfig.spatialhud.option.showPa: Draw the subtle translucent backing behind the selected lower-HUD surface. Methods 2 and 3 put this backing into the same private texture as the icons and text, so it receives exactly the same projective or world-space deformation. The full-width green, blue, or red method band remains as an identity marker even when this backing is hidden.
text.autoconfig.spatialhud.option.onlyDu: Keep the spatial presentation out of inventories, chat, pause menus, Mod Menu, and other screens. This is recommended for normal play. Texture methods enforce the same screen-open boundary even if this option is turned off, because they intentionally capture gameplay HUD roots only.
text.autoconfig.spatialhud.option.render: Choose the presentation of the already-forced captured HUD texture, not the HUD contents. All three modes use the same physical waist-height flat-map placement and are visible whenever that finite surface intersects the viewport—there is no fixed look-down gate and no unwarped HUD mode. A full-width colour band makes the active mode obvious: green Method 1 is a balanced forced mesh warp, blue Method 2 is a deliberately strong forced mesh warp, and red Method 3 draws that captured source rectangle on a real world quad with optional terrain depth. No method captures screens, chat, maps, debug text, or unrelated mod GUIs.
text.autoconfig.spatialhud.option.distan: Shared placement distance in block-like units, measured forward from the player-local panel origin. Methods 1 and 2 remain camera-yaw anchored while Method 3 uses the selected Method 3 anchor below. Increasing this makes the panel appear farther away and smaller in perspective; extremely low values are clamped to keep the plane in front of the camera.
text.autoconfig.spatialhud.option.planeW: Physical width of the complete captured panel, including the hotbar and surrounding selected roots. The height is derived from the HUD capture envelope so aspect ratio stays intact. This is a geometric size control shared by all three methods, not a separate scale for each HUD element.
text.autoconfig.spatialhud.option.virtua: Move the panel sideways within its active horizontal anchor. Positive values move right and negative values move left. With Method 3 set to Camera Yaw, right and left follow the view; with Player Body, they follow the body heading instead.

Move the whole panel up or down relative to eye height. Negative values place it at waist height, as if a flat Minecraft map rests in front of you; positive values raise it. This changes position only—use the three rotation controls below to change the surface itself.
text.autoconfig.spatialhud.option.minimu: This old JSON field is no longer used. Spatial HUD now culls only from real physical depth and viewport intersection, never from a configured camera-pitch cutoff.
text.autoconfig.spatialhud.option.virtua: Primary Flat-Map Tilt — Left ↔ Right Axis

Rotate the surface around its own left-to-right axis. The 85 degree default is almost horizontal, like a Minecraft map laid flat and viewed from above. Lower values create a deliberately steeper paper-like angle. Green Method 1 applies a balanced captured mesh warp, blue Method 2 forces a stronger captured mesh warp, and red Method 3 uses normal world perspective. This is a physical surface angle, not a camera-follow setting.
Fine Tilt Offset — Left ↔ Right Axis

Small additional rotation around the same left-to-right axis as Primary Flat-Map Tilt. Positive values push the far/top edge farther away; negative values pull it closer. Leave this at 0 unless fine-tuning the primary tilt, so the two controls do not unintentionally cancel each other.

Rotate the complete flat map around the player-local vertical up axis. Positive values turn its right edge farther forward and its left edge closer; negative values do the opposite. This is not camera yaw: it deliberately angles the surface left or right within the active horizontal anchor.

Rotate around the axis perpendicular to the paper surface. Positive values raise the right edge and lower the left edge; negative values reverse that slope. It is provided for deliberate three-axis adjustment, but 0 keeps text level and is the recommended normal-play value.
text.autoconfig.spatialhud.option.worldS: Applies only to red Method 3. Camera Yaw keeps the physical plane in front while looking left or right, matching Methods 1 and 2. Player Body keeps it at body heading instead, so it can remain at the side while the camera looks elsewhere. This setting is ignored by Methods 1 and 2.

Applies only to red Method 3. When enabled, the HUD texture uses the world depth buffer, so terrain or a block between the camera and the plane hides it like a physical object. Disable it to retain the world-space position but draw the panel visibly through terrain. This setting is ignored by Methods 1 and 2.
text.autoconfig.spatialhud.option.preser: Keep Companion Bars Native in Method 1

Compatibility fallback for green Classic Affine, disabled by default. Health, armor, hunger, and air normally travel with the spatial panel in all methods. Enable this only if AppleSkin, Detail Armor Bar Reconstructed, or a similar companion mod produces detached or duplicate status decorations; it leaves the complete affected status roots at their native location in Method 1 only.
text.autoconfig.spatialhud.option.showHo: Include the hotbar plus the vanilla spectator menu and spectator tooltip in the spatial panel. Disable this if another HUD mod owns the hotbar or if you want Spatial HUD to present only the status information around it.
text.autoconfig.spatialhud.option.showBa: Include the main vanilla status-bar roots: armor, health, hunger, and air. The enlarged lower-HUD source surface carries these roots alongside the hotbar, experience, and held-item information. Decorations injected into selected roots are captured with them in the texture methods; the Method 1 compatibility fallback above is off by default.
text.autoconfig.spatialhud.option.showXp: Include the vanilla experience progress bar, level number, and adjacent information-bar root. Disable it when another mod supplies a replacement experience display or when a cleaner hotbar-only panel is preferred.
text.autoconfig.spatialhud.option.showMo: Include the vanilla mount-health root while riding an entity. It has no effect while no mount-health HUD is active.
text.autoconfig.spatialhud.option.showHe: Include the transient selected-item name above the lower HUD panel. Disable it if a tooltip or inventory mod already provides a preferred held-item label.
